newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas falls in winter, Q4 sold aggressively.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas falls in winter, Q4 sold aggressively.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices fell in the coming winter on Wednesday, with the fourth quarter driven down as one company sold aggressively.
One large trader sold Q4 all the way down from 13.40 pence a therm to 13.20 pence, but then stopped. "It was very very difficult to find bids after that," said the seller.

Another trader pointed out that the fourth quarter had gone from around 12.50 pence to "damn near 13.50 pence" over the last two weeks or so, and it was not surprising to see prices coming off. "There's a bit of profit taking," he said.
"It might be profit taking. But there's also a lack of support. The market is so thin that it can be moved around by a couple of players," said another dealer.

As well as weakness in Q4, the first quarter next year was also off. The only trade seen was done at 16.80 pence a therm, but prices slipped later with offers coming from 16.75 pence by the close and bids no better than 16.65 pence or 16.60 pence, a broker said.
And the gas year from October 1997 was also weaker. "It was bearish in the morning and it quickly ran down 0.10 pence in the gas year," said a trader.
Most of the activity seen took place in the morning. The aggressive seller of Q4 said their selling started at around 0830 GMT, and was mostly finished by lunchtime.
An industry meeting on a standardised NBP contract kept many players out of the office in the afternoon. One player described the afternoon session as "a bit of a non-event."

As well as trade in the winter, there was active trade in the prompt market, including within day, day ahead and trade for the next two days, as well as some interest for single month deals in August, September and October.
There was also trade seen as far forward as the 1998 gas year, running to September 1999, as well as deals in the summer of 1998.
While the OTC market was reasonably active, futures suffered their first really slow day for over a week. Only one trade, for 25 lots, was done, in March at 14.10 pence a therm, down by 0.20 pence.
